1	# Localization construction and verification
2	
3	Use public APIs from the installed package, through `unity-cli editor eval`.
4	Keep calls synchronous and short; query async completion in subsequent calls.
5	Inspect `unity-cli tool schema eval_csharp` and `get_ui_element_state` before
6	constructing payloads. A transport success containing a tool error is failure.
7	
8	## Package and assets
9	
10	Inspect package metadata before choosing a version. The Unity 2022.3 manual lists
11	Localization 1.4.4; the registry can recommend a later compatible version.
12	Do not assume a Unity 6 package works on an older Editor.
13	Use `package_manager install`, then wait for ping, `isCompiling:false`,
14	`isUpdating:false`, resolved package version and console checks.
15	
16	Choose a scoped folder, such as `Assets/Localization/Demo`. In repository E2E,
17	use `Assets/Scenes/Generated/E2E/Localization` for generated scenes/assets.
18	Inspect existing settings before creating any asset. Use
19	`LocalizationEditorSettings.ActiveLocalizationSettings` to select an existing
20	settings asset, or persist a new `LocalizationSettings` asset and assign it.
21	Do not replace an existing project's startup selectors or Addressables groups.
22	
23	For each requested code, use `Locale.CreateLocale("en")` / `("ja")` only when
24	that locale is absent, save it with `AssetDatabase.CreateAsset`, then register
25	it with `LocalizationEditorSettings.AddLocale`. Verify both are available.
26	
27	Use `LocalizationEditorSettings.GetStringTableCollection(name)` to detect an
28	existing collection. Otherwise call `CreateStringTableCollection(name, folder,
29	locales)`. This handles shared data and Addressables registration; creating loose
30	`StringTable` objects does not establish the complete collection. Use
31	`collection.GetTable(locale.Identifier)`, add a missing locale table when needed,
32	and call `StringTable.AddEntry(key, translation)`. Mark changed tables and
33	`SharedData` dirty, then `AssetDatabase.SaveAssets`. Read back matching shared key
34	IDs and each exact translation. Example values: key `greeting`, English
35	`Hello, world!`, Japanese `こんにちは、世界！`.
36	
37	## Persistent UI binding
38	
39	Use the requested UGUI Text or TextMeshPro label. Assign its compatible font
40	asset with Japanese glyph coverage before judging the translation. A correct
41	`text` property with square replacement glyphs is not a successful visual check.
42	
43	Add/reuse `UnityEngine.Localization.Components.LocalizeStringEvent`. Configure
44	`StringReference.TableReference` and `TableEntryReference` with the persisted
45	collection and key. Wire its `OnUpdateString` to the text property setter using
46	`UnityEditor.Events.UnityEventTools.AddPersistentListener<string>` and a
47	`UnityEngine.Events.UnityAction<string>` targeting that setter. A temporary
48	`AddListener` lambda disappears on scene reload. Do not remove other listeners
49	or add a duplicate when retrying. Mark the component/scene dirty and save.
50	
51	Reload the scene in Edit Mode. Read the persistent event target/method, table
52	and key, and saved translations before entering Play. Do not replace a dirty
53	user scene without preserving its changes.
54	
55	## Runtime proof
56	
57	1. Enter Play. Wait for initialization completion and successful operation status;
58	   if it fails, inspect missing settings, locales and Addressables diagnostics.
59	   Do not block the main thread with a sleep or an async wait inside eval.
60	2. Set `LocalizationSettings.SelectedLocale` using
61	   `AvailableLocales.GetLocale("en")`; fail if it returns null.
62	3. Poll `get_ui_element_state` for the specific label until its actual `text`
63	   equals `Hello, world!`. Use a bounded deadline and allow frames between polls.
64	4. Capture Game view with `osFallback:false`; inspect the returned image.
65	5. Set the selected locale to `ja`, wait for `こんにちは、世界！`, and capture
66	   with identical camera/resolution. Inspect that the text is visible and legible.
67	6. Switch back to `en` and verify the original label text. Read console errors,
68	   stop Play and verify the saved assets and persistent event again.
69	
70	Do not use direct text assignment, editor preview alone or a String Database
71	lookup as proof of the live binding. If a Game capture omits overlay UI, retain
72	that failure and consult the separate capture issue #422. Through `editor eval`,
73	open the Game view with `EditorApplication.ExecuteMenuItem("Window/General/Game")`
74	and call `UnityEngine.ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshot(absolutePngPath)` in Play.
75	Wait for a rendered frame and the file to finish writing before reading it.
76	Keep Game resolution fixed for both locales and inspect the resulting images;
77	this captures actual Game UI, not a constructed image or OS-window fallback.
78	Persist image paths, label state, versions,
79	saved Locale/table assets and the tool transcript as evidence.
80	
81	## API references and authorship
82	
83	This workflow is independently authored from the repository tool contract and
84	Unity's public package APIs, without official unity-agent-plugin skill content.
85	
86	- [Localization Editor APIs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@1.4/api/UnityEditor.Localization.LocalizationEditorSettings.html)
87	- [Localize String Event](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@1.4/api/UnityEngine.Localization.Components.LocalizeStringEvent.html)
88	- [Unity 2022.3 package compatibility](https://docs.unity3d.com/2022.3/Documentation/Manual/com.unity.localization.html)

1	# Runtime Checklist
2	
3	## Binary Selection
4	
5	- Prefer an installed `unity-cli` binary when it exists on `PATH` (the installer links it to `~/.local/bin/unity-cli`).
6	- If no binary is installed, run `scripts/install.sh` (macOS / Linux) or `scripts/install.ps1` (Windows, when published) instead of asking the user.
7	- Only inside a unity-cli source checkout, `cargo run -- <args>` is a development alternative.
8	
9	## Project Setup
10	
11	- `unity-cli setup` = binary check → `bridge install` → Editor `ping`; it prints one JSON report and exits non-zero until the Editor answers for this project.
12	- Tell the user before running it: it edits `Packages/manifest.json` and, when the project uses only the legacy Input Manager and the Editor is closed, sets `activeInputHandler: 2` (Both) in `ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset` so the Input System dependency does not block the Editor with a restart dialog. `bridge install` is idempotent (a second run leaves both files byte-identical).
13	- If the Editor was already open, it may show "enable the Input System backends? (restart)"; bridge commands time out until someone answers it. Close the Editor and rerun `setup --launch-editor` instead.
14	- `--launch-editor` starts the Unity Hub Editor recorded in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` (`UNITY_EDITOR_PATH` overrides) and waits up to 900 s (`--wait-secs`).
15	- `editor.projectMatches: false` means another project's Editor owns the port; pass `--port`.
16	- `versionCheck.status: mismatch` (from `setup` or `system ping`) → `unity-cli bridge upgrade`, or update the CLI.
17	- Verify the binary with `unity-cli --version` before debugging higher-level workflows.
18	
19	## Instance Selection
20	
21	- Use `unity-cli system ping` when a single active target is expected.
22	- Use `unity-cli instances list` when multiple editors may be running.
23	- Prefer `--project-path <project>` (or running inside the project) to target one Editor; `AMBIGUOUS_EDITOR` lists candidates in `data.candidates`.
24	- Use `unity-cli instances set-active <host:port>` only after confirming the target is `up`.
25	
26	## Command Routing
27	
28	- The bootstrap-relevant typed subcommands are `system ping`, `scene create`, `instances list`, `instances set-active`. Use them when available. (`instances list` / `instances set-active` are local registry operations rather than bridge-tool wrappers.)
29	- The `reference *` family (`fetch`, `status`, `search`, `grep`, `view`, `find-symbol`, `diff`, `resolve-symbol-at`, `embed-build`, `embed-search`, `clean`) also has typed wrappers over the `reference_*` bridge tools — see the `unity-csharp-reference` skill. Beyond these, most bridge tools have no typed wrapper.
30	- For every tool without a typed wrapper, use `unity-cli raw <tool_name> --json '{...}'` (or its alias `unity-cli tool call <tool_name> --json '{...}'`). This is the primary invocation pattern, not a fallback — bridge tools such as `analyze_scene_contents`, `find_by_component`, `modify_component`, and `get_compilation_state` are all invoked this way.
31	- Discover tools with `unity-cli tool list --query <term> --compact`; add `--category <name>` (a `docs/tools.md` heading or slug such as `scenes`, `playback-testing`) and `--limit N` / `--offset N` to keep output small. Inspect a tool's expected JSON payload with `unity-cli tool schema <tool_name> --output json`.
32	- Use `--output json` when another tool or script will consume the result.
33	
34	## Connection Recovery
35	
36	- A failed `system ping` does not prove the Editor is closed. Run `unity-cli doctor --output json` (add `--project-path <dir>` outside the project) before any fallback such as hand-editing YAML.
37	- Act on the `diagnosis` code:
38	  - `SAFE_MODE` / `COMPILE_ERRORS`: the bridge is not loaded. Fix each `editorLog.compileErrors[]` entry (`file`, `line`, `code`) by editing the file directly, then let Unity recompile or restart the Editor.
39	  - `BRIDGE_NOT_INSTALLED`: run `unity-cli setup` (or `unity-cli bridge install`) to add `com.akiojin.unity-cli-bridge` to `Packages/manifest.json`.
40	  - `PORT_IN_USE`: `port.listenerPid` / `port.listenerProcess` hold the port. Stop it or change the bridge port and pass the same `--port`.
41	  - `EDITOR_NOT_RUNNING`: start the Editor for the project and wait for import to finish.
42	  - `SANDBOX_BLOCKED`: the local socket was denied. Retry in a permitted execution context according to the host's approval policy; do not bypass sandbox restrictions or conclude the Editor is missing. If reachability still cannot be verified, ask the user to confirm the running project and bridge connection before considering an offline fallback.
43	  - `BRIDGE_NOT_RESPONDING`: the Editor is still importing/compiling or the port differs from Project Settings > Unity CLI Bridge.
44	- Re-run `unity-cli doctor` until `diagnosis` is `OK`, then continue the workflow.
45	- An empty instance list or failed process probe inside a sandbox is also inconclusive. Confirm the project/host/port and the user's Editor state instead of treating restricted visibility as `EDITOR_NOT_RUNNING`.
46	- When the target Editor is reachable, never hand-edit serialized `.unity`, `.prefab`, or `.asset` YAML. Bridge operations keep serialized references, prefab overrides, and the live Editor state in sync.
47	- If recovery cannot restore the connection and offline work is appropriate, declare the fallback before editing: explain the verified limitation, affected files, alternative method, and how the result will be checked after reopening Unity. Without confirmation of an uncertain sandbox diagnosis, pause dependent edits. Do not silently substitute YAML edits for bridge calls.
48	
49	## CI Notes
50	
51	- Set `UNITY_CLI_HOST` and `UNITY_CLI_PORT` explicitly in CI.
52	- Keep JSON payloads quoted as a single shell argument.
53	- If connectivity fails in CI, report the resolved host and port before retrying.

#!/bin/bash
# run a C# statements file through eval_csharp (transcript-logged)
F=/tmp/issue381/2022.3.62f3/final-evidence
J=$(jq -Rs "{code: ., mode: \"statements\"}" < "$1")

--- step.sh
#!/bin/bash
# step.sh <code> <expected> <label>: select locale via LocalizationSettings.SelectedLocale, poll the actual UI label text
F=/tmp/issue381/2022.3.62f3/final-evidence; U=$F/u.sh
code=$1; expected=$2; label=$3
J=$(jq -n --arg c "if (!UnityEditor.EditorApplication.isPlaying) return \"FAIL: not playing\"; var l = UnityEngine.Localization.Settings.LocalizationSettings.AvailableLocales.GetLocale(\"$code\"); if (l == null) return \"FAIL: locale $code not available\"; UnityEngine.Localization.Settings.LocalizationSettings.SelectedLocale = l; return \"selected=\" + UnityEngine.Localization.Settings.LocalizationSettings.SelectedLocale.Identifier.Code;" "{code:\$c, mode:\"statements\"}")
sel=$($U raw eval_csharp --json "$J" --output json | jq -c "{state,exception,value}")
echo "$sel"
ok=false
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  st=$($U raw get_ui_element_state --json "{\"elementPath\":\"/LocalizationCanvas/Greeting\"}" --output json)
  actual=$(echo "$st" | jq -r .text)
  if [ "$actual" = "$expected" ]; then ok=true; break; fi
  sleep 0.5
done
jq -n --arg step "$label" --arg code "$code" --arg expected "$expected" --arg actual "$actual" --argjson match $ok --argjson polls $i --argjson select "$sel" --argjson state "$st" --arg at "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "{step:\$step, locale:\$code, expected:\$expected, actual:\$actual, match:\$match, polls:\$polls, selectResult:\$select, uiElementState:\$state, observedAt:\$at}" | tee $F/$label.json
$ok

--- shot.sh
#!/bin/bash
# shot.sh <name>: documented fallback — Game view opened via menu, UnityEngine.ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshot(absolute PNG) in Play
F=/tmp/issue381/2022.3.62f3/final-evidence; U=$F/u.sh
out=$F/$1.png
[ -e "$out" ] && { echo "FAIL: $out already exists, refusing to overwrite"; exit 1; }
J=$(jq -n --arg c "if (!UnityEditor.EditorApplication.isPlaying) return \"FAIL: not playing\"; var opened = UnityEditor.EditorApplication.ExecuteMenuItem(\"Window/General/Game\"); var sz = UnityEditor.Handles.GetMainGameViewSize(); UnityEngine.ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshot(\"$out\"); return \"requested menu=\" + opened + \" gameView=\" + sz.x + \"x\" + sz.y + \" screen=\" + UnityEngine.Screen.width + \"x\" + UnityEngine.Screen.height + \" focused=\" + (UnityEditor.EditorWindow.focusedWindow == null ? \"null\" : UnityEditor.EditorWindow.focusedWindow.GetType().Name) + \" frame=\" + UnityEngine.Time.frameCount;" "{code:\$c, mode:\"statements\"}")
req=$($U raw eval_csharp --json "$J" --output json | jq -c "{state,exception,value}"); echo "$req"
prev=-1
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 0.5
  [ -s "$out" ] || continue
  cur=$(stat -f %z "$out"); [ "$cur" = "$prev" ] && break; prev=$cur
done

## Integration verification summary (Unity 2022.3.62f3, port 6507)

Localization passes, and the primary `capture_screenshot` now includes the Screen Space Overlay label — but only when the Editor is the frontmost macOS app. With the Editor in the background it fails with `GAME_VIEW_NOT_FOCUSED`, and those failures are retained.

I wrote the report to `integration-evidence/report.json` rather than `final-evidence/report.json`, because that file already holds the prior fallback run and you asked not to overwrite earlier evidence.

### Localization
- **Persistence:** the scene reload in Edit Mode reads back the same settings, `en`/`ja` Locales, `DemoStrings` entries and one persistent `UnityEngine.UI.Text.set_text` listener, before Play and after each Play session. The saved asset files are byte-identical before and after.
- **Live label:** `get_ui_element_state` returned `Hello, world!` → `こんにちは、世界！` → `Hello, world!` using only `SelectedLocale`; no label text was written.
- **Two failed polls, retained:** `40_play_ja_state.json` and `p2_20_play_en_state.json` did not match because the Play loop was frozen at the time (see side effects below). Both resolved without re-setting anything once frames resumed.
- **Console:** 0 errors, exceptions or asserts before, during and after; nothing was cleared. No Search indexer exception exists in this Editor session (console and `editor.log`), so there was nothing to preserve separately.

### Primary capture (PR #429)

| Editor state | Result |
|---|---|
| Frontmost | Success, "Composited Game View screenshot captured successfully", 1280x720 |
| Background | `GAME_VIEW_NOT_FOCUSED`, no image (5 occurrences) |

- **Frontmost images, inspected:** en shows `Hello, world!`; ja shows `こんにちは、世界！` with all glyphs, no replacement boxes. They are byte-identical to the prior run's fallback images (en `17eed410…`, ja `c4811c33…`).
- **Why background fails:** the handler needs `EditorWindow.focusedWindow` to be the Game view, and that is null whenever Unity is not the active app. `Window/General/Game` and `manage_windows focus` (which reports success) do not change it.
- **One transient failure while frontmost:** the first attempt right after activation still returned `GAME_VIEW_NOT_FOCUSED`; the next attempt succeeded. I did not determine why.
- **Fallback:** the documented `ScreenCapture` fallback produced a correct en image with the Editor in the background, and a correct ja image with the Editor frontmost (identical to the primary ja capture); there is no valid background ja fallback image in this run. Two fallback images taken during the frozen loop are stale and labelled as such in the report.

- **Asset refresh:** the Editor was still running the bridge DLL built at 18:05:56 and did not recompile the refreshed sources (18:20:09) during a 45 s wait. I issued `refresh_assets`; it rebuilt at 18:23:00 with 0 errors.

- **Background Play now stalls:** after being frontmost once, this Editor freezes the Play loop whenever it is in the background (`runInBackground=False`). Later unattended runs on this Editor process will hang at initialization until it is frontmost or restarted.
- **Bridge `.meta` files:** the refresh made Unity rewrite 43 guid-only `.cs.meta` files into full metas (same GUIDs). No `.cs` file changed.
